woods_bellhouse_entry.body: The old path bell hangs above a cottage whose doorstep has sunk beneath the roots. Someone is ringing it from below. A Fairy on the lintel points at a loose floorboard, then puts a finger to its lips; the occupant has finally fallen asleep.

choices.label: Lift the board without waking anyone
choices.outcome: Your companion steadies the board while you ease it free. A warm draught smells of bread and wet wool.

choices.label: Sound the bell once to announce yourself
choices.outcome: One careful note answers from underneath the house. The Fairy shows you which floorboards carry the sound.

woods_bellhouse_cellar.body: Below the cottage, a bellkeeper has built shelves around a tree root instead of cutting it. The root is tapping the bell rope whenever water reaches an old drainage bowl. Her kettle is balanced on a history book, and both are getting damp.

choices.label: Move the bowl and brace its channel
choices.outcome: Mud fills your sleeves, but the bowl settles under a stone brace. The tapping stops long enough for the keeper to find her boots.
choices.description: Pay 3% HP; no knockouts; Temporary team defense +5%.

choices.label: Trace the root before moving anything
choices.outcome: You mark the places where the root drinks. A shallow groove can lead the water away without stripping its bark.

woods_bellhouse_belfry.body: A ladder reaches the belfry through the cottage chimney. From here, you can see that the bell rope brushes three nesting cups, each woven by a different Fairy. The keeper offers a choice: a louder warning for travellers, or a quieter house for its smallest tenants.

choices.label: Pad the rope around the nests
choices.outcome: The bell gives a soft, clear note. The keeper writes your name beside the nests in her maintenance book.

choices.label: Move the pull to the public path
choices.outcome: Travellers can reach the pull without crossing the roof. The keeper promises to mention who made the change.
choices.description: +5% of the run reward; World remembers.

woods_reedwheel_entry.body: A wooden mill turns although the stream beside it is almost dry. Small cups on the wheel catch falling leaves, and each cup knocks a different note from the spokes. A Goblin miller is listening with both hands over his floury ears.

choices.label: Help him separate the notes
choices.outcome: Your companion waits beside each spoke as you tap it. The miller finds the note that keeps getting lost.

choices.label: Catch the leaves before they jam the wheel
choices.outcome: You clear a path through the cups. The wheel finds a steady rhythm and the miller finally uncovers his ears.

woods_reedwheel_race.body: Behind the mill, a split water race feeds a kitchen garden on one side and a muddy Slime nursery on the other. A fallen branch has diverted everything toward the cabbages. Tiny round faces watch from a puddle that is becoming more flour than water.

choices.label: Reopen both channels by hand
choices.outcome: Cold water runs up your sleeves. Your companion settles beside the smallest Slime until the returning trickle reaches it.
choices.description: Pay 3% HP; no knockouts; Lead bond +1.

choices.label: Build a temporary leaf spillway
choices.outcome: The broad leaves carry water around the blockage. Sorting their supports leaves you a modest choice of useful woodland gatherings.
choices.description: Select the run's one material bundle.

woods_reedwheel_loft.body: The loft holds the miller's real project: shelves of labelled bird calls, rain rhythms and wind notes, written as marks on bark. He cannot decide whether the repaired wheel belongs in his archive or beside the path where other people can hear it.

choices.label: Write instructions for the next keeper
choices.outcome: You leave clear directions instead of a grand explanation. The miller hangs them where a shorter reader can reach.
choices.description: Use this run's research allowance; World remembers.

choices.label: Turn the listening bench toward the path
choices.outcome: You rest together while the wheel plays through its cups. The miller opens the shutters to anyone walking past.

woods_crooked_bridge_entry.body: A narrow bridge has a neat railing on its left side and an extravagant railing on its right. Two neighbours stand at opposite ends, each holding the last plank. Their companions have already crossed, met in the middle and decided to sit down together.

choices.label: Ask the companions where they crossed
choices.outcome: Following their muddy pawprints reveals a solid strip between the disputed railings. Neither neighbour can argue with the evidence.

choices.label: Measure the bridge before choosing a side
choices.outcome: The left posts are straight and the right joints are strong. You draw a design that needs both neighbours.

woods_crooked_bridge_middle.body: The missing plank lies above a shallow patch of nettles. From the gap, you can see that one neighbour has been leaving tools beneath the other's railing, where rain cannot reach them. Both call this an accident when you point it out.

choices.label: Hold the plank while they fit its ends
choices.outcome: The nettles catch your ankles, but both neighbours take the weight before your arms tire. The joint seats cleanly.
choices.description: Pay 3% HP; no knockouts; Temporary team defense +5%.

choices.label: Sort the sheltered tools into shared bundles
choices.outcome: You keep their working tools together and separate only loose, useful offcuts. Cooperation suddenly looks less like surrender.
choices.description: Select the run's one material bundle.

woods_crooked_bridge_farbank.body: The last task is a sign. Each neighbour has brought a name for the bridge, written in letters too large for the available board. Their companions remain shoulder to shoulder beneath it, perfectly content to wait while the humans catch up.

choices.label: Name the bridge after the meeting place
choices.outcome: You write Middle in small letters. Both neighbours find room for their names underneath, as builders rather than owners.

choices.label: Leave the name blank and mark safe footing
choices.outcome: The sign explains where to step in heavy rain. The neighbours agree that a useful sign can wait for a name.

woods_toast_basket_entry.body: A covered basket hangs just beyond reach, suspended from a branch bent by last night's rain. A Goblin cook has left a note asking whoever finds it to save the toast from the ants. Your companion can smell warm herbs beneath the cloth.

choices.label: Lower the basket and share a quiet break
choices.outcome: You lower it slowly enough to keep the cups upright. The cook has packed more food than one traveller could reasonably need.

choices.label: Return the basket to the dry stone table
choices.outcome: Your companion guards the table while you straighten the cloth. You leave the cook a dry place to begin again.

woods_blue_chalk_entry.body: Blue chalk footprints cross the path, climb a tree and end halfway up empty air. A Pixie schoolmaster is searching the ground for the rest of his lesson. He insists it was a very ordinary lesson about directions until his pupils began improving it.

choices.label: Draw a route everyone can follow
choices.outcome: You connect the wandering marks with arrows at ground level. The schoolmaster admits that directions should account for the person receiving them.

choices.label: Follow the prints into a practice clearing
choices.outcome: The pupils gather at the clearing's edge and call for a friendly demonstration. Your team has time to prepare before the lesson begins.

woods_copper_stump_entry.body: Copper nails cover a stump beside the path. Each holds a scrap recording a small borrowed thing: a cup, a ribbon, half an afternoon. A new scrap bears your companion's pawprint, although neither of you remembers agreeing to lend anything.

choices.label: Read the earliest receipts together
choices.outcome: The oldest entries record help rather than debt. You copy the system before rain turns the remaining ink green.

choices.label: Add one hour of freely given help
choices.outcome: You pull weeds around the stump without adding a price. A loose receipt flutters down, leaving your companion's pawprint unencumbered.

woods_moth_press_entry.body: A ranger kneels beside a flower press full of very patient moths. She opened it to show a visitor some leaves, and the moths mistook its warm pages for shelter. Now a pressing appointment is approaching, but she refuses to close the cover.

choices.label: Make a shady shelter beside the press
choices.outcome: You fold broad leaves into a roof. The moths move of their own accord, leaving the pages free and the ranger visibly relieved.

choices.label: Study the leaves while everyone waits
choices.outcome: The ranger shows you how each leaf records its growing season. The moths eventually wander out across your notes.

encounters.title: A Coat with Room for Two

woods_raincoat_entry.body: A child has stretched a raincoat between two roots to shelter a Wisp. The Wisp does not appear troubled by water, but it stays under the coat whenever the child checks. Both are reluctant to admit that the storm has already passed.

choices.label: Sit with them until the last drops stop
choices.outcome: Your companion settles beneath the edge of the coat. The child finds room for everyone without being asked.

choices.label: Improve the little shelter before leaving
choices.outcome: You secure the coat where a new shower will not pull it loose. The Wisp marks the entrance with a gentle glow.

woods_tree_letters_entry.body: A loose flap of bark conceals a letter addressed to the next person who bothers to look. Its writer asks only whether the footpath still reaches the river. A pencilled return address points to a house that has become part of the tree.

choices.label: Write a careful description of the present path
choices.outcome: You describe the turn by the white stone and the place where the roots rise. There is finally something honest to send.
choices.description: Use this run's research allowance; World remembers.

choices.label: Draw the river instead of giving directions
choices.outcome: Your companion leaves a muddy mark beside your drawing. It looks enough like a greeting that you keep it.

woods_stone_calendar_entry.body: Flat stones around a spring carry notches for days of sunshine. None has a mark for rain, though every fern nearby has flourished in it. An old caretaker offers you the chisel, then admits that the missing category has troubled him for years.

choices.label: Add a small mark for useful rain
choices.outcome: The first new notch fills immediately with clear water. The caretaker begins counting the garden's good days again.
choices.description: Use this run's research allowance; World remembers.

choices.label: Clear the spring's buried overflow
choices.outcome: Wet grit works into your sleeves before the overflow clears. After washing, the team rests beside water that can move freely.
choices.description: Pay 3% HP; no knockouts; Heal surviving team 10%.

woods_teapot_entry.body: A chipped teapot steams on a mossy altar, though its lid reveals nothing inside. The steam smells faintly different to each member of your team. A nearby inscription asks visitors to leave the smell of a place they would like to reach again.

choices.label: Remember home together
choices.outcome: You sit long enough for the steam to smell like a familiar doorway. Even your most watchful companion lets its shoulders relax.

choices.label: Describe the scent in your journal
choices.outcome: The words are less precise than the smell, but they preserve what each companion noticed. You leave the lid properly seated.

encounters.title: The Race with No Finish Line

woods_crooked_race_entry.body: Several woodland beasts wait beside a line of fallen petals. Their course circles a stump, crosses the path and loops back into its own starting place. A spectator has brought an enormous ribbon and no convincing explanation of where it should go.

choices.label: Volunteer your team for the opening heat
choices.outcome: Two eager challengers take their places. The others clear the course and wait for your signal before the friendly contest begins.

choices.label: Help the spectators mark a proper finish
choices.outcome: You lay the ribbon across a straight stretch of ground. The cheering becomes much easier to understand.

woods_root_classroom_entry.body: A Dryad teaches beneath a tree whose roots form rows of benches. The smallest seats have disappeared under summer growth, leaving the younger pupils peering between their elders. The teacher has stopped the lesson rather than let anyone spend it staring at somebody else's back.

choices.label: Rearrange the class into a circle
choices.outcome: Your companion takes the lowest place beside the smallest pupil. Suddenly everyone can see the leaf the teacher is holding.

choices.label: Observe how the roots share their space
choices.outcome: The roots bend around old stones instead of breaking them. You sketch a lesson the teacher had not planned to give.

woods_pool_bell_entry.body: The bellkeeper you met beneath the cottage is washing cups at the pool. She recognizes your companion before she recognizes you. A traveller has heard the improved bell but wants to know whether it means welcome, warning, or simply that somebody is awake.

choices.label: Help her write a clear signal guide
choices.outcome: You choose three short patterns that cannot be mistaken for one another. She hangs the guide beside the public path.

choices.label: Carry the welcome signal to the nearest crossing
choices.outcome: Your companion keeps pace while you explain the note at each turning. Travellers begin answering it with raised hands.

woods_seedling_score_entry.body: Beside the reopened listening mill, seedlings lean toward the sound of the wheel. The miller has arranged his pots in rows and is taking the experiment much too seriously. He asks whether music helps them grow, or whether this window simply has better light.

choices.label: Compare the sunny and shaded rows
choices.outcome: You move only the labels, leaving the seedlings undisturbed. The miller agrees to keep useful notes rather than announce a miracle.

choices.label: Help carry the crowded pots outside
choices.outcome: The pots are heavier than they look. You sort loose woodland gatherings while making room for the roots to spread.
choices.description: Pay 3% HP; no knockouts; Select the run's one material bundle.

encounters.title: The Shadow That Stayed for Lunch

woods_borrowed_shadow_entry.body: Your companion's shadow remains seated when the rest of the team moves on. A Pixie is holding its edge beneath a picnic cloth to keep the plates from sliding. It looks embarrassed when it realizes the practical arrangement has acquired an owner.

choices.label: Trade a flat stone for the shadow
choices.outcome: The Pixie tests the stone twice before letting go. Your companion's shadow hurries back without commenting on its afternoon.

choices.label: Invite the Pixie to explain the trick
choices.outcome: It demonstrates using its own shadow this time. You note where the light falls and leave the picnic upright.

encounters.title: The Boat That Grew a Branch

woods_log_raft_entry.body: A makeshift raft has become a small floating garden. The branch used as its steering pole has rooted in the deck, trapping it against a bend. A courier on the bank must choose between delivering dry letters and keeping this stubborn little tree alive.

choices.label: Guide the raft around the bend from shore
choices.outcome: A wet rope rubs your palms, but the rooted deck moves into open water. The courier can continue without cutting the branch.
choices.description: Pay 3% HP; no knockouts; +5% of the run reward.

choices.label: Move the letters to the sheltered footpath
choices.outcome: You show the courier where the bank stays high. The raft can remain a garden without becoming a failed delivery.

encounters.title: A Name That Was Sewn Twice

woods_worn_collar_entry.body: A retired trail guide has brought a worn collar to the bridge you helped inspect. Two names are sewn inside it, one above the other. She cannot remember which belonged to her first companion and which was the name the neighbours used for her.

choices.label: Listen while she follows the old route in memory
choices.outcome: At the familiar turn, she remembers who used to answer which name. She keeps both stitches where they are.

choices.label: Record her route before the details wander
choices.outcome: You sketch the crossings as she describes them. She corrects the direction of a hill and signs both names underneath.

woods_chalk_path_entry.body: A messenger sits beside the tree that held the hidden letter. Your reply has been copied onto a sheet large enough to survive the journey. The messenger needs either a clear route through the roots or a sheltered place to wait out another shower.

choices.label: Show the messenger the river turning
choices.outcome: You walk as far as the white stone. The messenger leaves with the reply folded safely inside a dry sleeve.
choices.description: +5% of the run reward; World remembers.

choices.label: Prepare a covered resting place
choices.outcome: You finish the shelter while the messenger wraps the letter. The reply will travel after the rain instead of through it.

woods_late_breakfast_entry.body: The cook whose basket you returned has laid a breakfast table beside the path. One place remains empty because nobody knows how much room to leave for your companion. He has tried a cushion, a crate and a very dignified upturned flowerpot.

choices.label: Let your companion choose its own place
choices.outcome: The choice surprises the cook, who moves the entire table rather than disturb a comfortable guest. Breakfast finally begins.

choices.label: Share a slow meal before the next turn
choices.outcome: The cook brings warm water and a sensible portion for each traveller. Nobody is hurried away from the table.

woods_familiar_leaf_drift_entry.body: New leaves collect at the familiar stepping stones after every shower. Nothing here needs rescuing forever; the current simply changes its mind about where to carry them. Today a thick mat hides the middle stone, and your companion is considering a very optimistic jump.

choices.label: Clear a narrow channel through the leaves
choices.outcome: Cold water reaches your knees before the channel opens. The middle stone emerges with enough room for careful feet.
choices.description: Pay 3% HP; no knockouts; +5% of the run reward.

choices.label: Take the marked bank path together
choices.outcome: You give the optimistic jumper time to reconsider. The bank path offers a dry crossing and an excellent view of the leaves.

woods_familiar_ring_entry.body: Fresh pawprints circle the familiar woodland practice ring. Its usual residents come and go, and today's challengers have arranged fallen cones along the boundary. They pause when they see your team, leaving the entrance open and the decision plainly in your hands.

choices.label: Accept a two-beast friendly challenge
choices.outcome: Two challengers step into the ring and wait. Your companions have space to take their places before the first move.

choices.label: Help reset the cones for the next visitors
choices.outcome: You straighten the widest gaps in the boundary. Watching the residents check your work sharpens the team's sense of spacing.

woods_familiar_fern_shelf_entry.body: The familiar fern shelf stays dry even when the path is damp. Somebody has left a new layer of soft leaves beneath its overhang, while the old ones have become part of the soil. Your companions recognize the spot and slow down without a command.

choices.label: Rest beneath the overhang
choices.outcome: You settle where the ground is firm. The small shelter gives everyone a chance to ease the journey out of tired limbs.

choices.label: Tidy the shelter for the next team
choices.outcome: Your companions hold the loose leaves while you sweep wet twigs away. You leave the entrance easier to find.

woods_familiar_windfalls_entry.body: A fresh windfall has scattered twigs, bark and tangled fibres across the familiar gathering path. The heap looks promising until movement beneath it reveals a patient Slime using the underside as a roof. Enough loose material remains outside its chosen room for careful hands.

choices.label: Gather only from the uncovered edges
choices.outcome: You sort useful pieces without shifting the roof. The Slime watches the pile grow tidier around its doorway.
choices.description: Select the run's one material bundle.

choices.label: Study how the fibres hold together
choices.outcome: Their crossings make a stronger mesh than their size suggests. You sketch the pattern and leave the shelter intact.

encounters.title: Familiar Territory · A Moving Sun Patch

woods_familiar_sun_patch_entry.body: The familiar sunny clearing has shifted its warmest patch to the far side of a fallen tree. A wild resident has claimed it for the afternoon and stamps a small challenge into the dust. There is plenty of shaded room to pass without disturbing the dispute.

choices.label: Offer a single friendly contest
choices.outcome: The resident leaves the warm patch and faces your team in the open clearing. Both sides have room to prepare.

choices.label: Lead the team through the cooler shade
choices.outcome: You watch the narrow gaps between roots as you pass. The team settles into a careful, compact travelling order.

encounters.title: Familiar Territory · Marks on the Rain Stone

woods_familiar_rain_measure_entry.body: Rain has climbed a little higher on the familiar measuring stone. Fresh wet marks cross old dry ones, making last week's confident predictions look rather foolish. The spring beside it is clear, and a small cup remains on its usual flat ledge.

choices.label: Measure today instead of correcting yesterday
choices.outcome: You add one honest observation beneath the others. The disagreement between marks becomes useful information instead of a mistake.

choices.label: Wash the dust from the team's feet
choices.outcome: You use the cup without muddying the spring. Clean feet make the next stretch feel less like an argument with the path.
